- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak or adjust downward after 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — adjust for gradual decay toward historical mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sharp downward trends after sentiment shifts; add a 5–10% downward buffer if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.5 to -0.2), model tends to ignore them; apply a “sentiment decay” multiplier (e.g., 0.85–0.90) to forecast weights.
